transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess the main thing that brings me in is that since I stopped working, I just can’t seem to slow down. I’m up and moving from one little job to the next all day long. It's honestly like I still have a crew waiting on me or something, even though I'm not on the clock anymore.
When you're keeping this pace, how would you describe your mood—do you feel unusually happy, excited, or perhaps more irritable than usual?

No, I wouldn't say I feel unusually happy or excited. And I'm not really irritable either. I just... I don't know, I just feel like I need to be doing something. It's not a mood thing, it's more like a habit I can't break. I just feel normal, but busy.

When you are doing these tasks, do you find yourself feeling like everything has to be done in a very specific, orderly way, or that you get frustrated if things aren't done exactly according to your plan?

No, not really. I don't care much about doing things in a specific order or having a strict plan. I just... I just do whatever catches my eye next. If I start fixing a hinge on a cabinet and then see the floor needs sweeping, I'll just go grab the broom. It doesn't bother me if things aren't perfect, I just need to be doing something.
Do you find that you spend a lot of your time feeling worried or anxious about various things in your life, even when you aren't busy with these tasks?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I worry about normal things, I guess, like anyone else, but I wouldn't say I spend a lot of time feeling anxious. It's really just the constant moving around and needing to stay busy. It's not like I'm pacing because I'm worried about something. I just... I just have a hard time sitting still.
Looking back at your childhood or your time in school, did you struggle with sitting still or staying focused on tasks back then, or is this something that only started recently?

No, it's definitely not a recent thing. It's been like this pretty much my whole life. Even way back in grade school, my teachers used to say I was a bright kid, but just... scattered. I was always losing my pencils, and I'd just call out answers in class without waiting my turn. They were always having to remind me to actually finish my work before I could go out for recess. So, yeah, the trouble sitting still and focusing, that's always been there.
